title: Clarify AI - Onramp & Routing SDK integration discovery
summary: Initial discovery on integrating Redwood for a hybrid deployment with focus on SDKs and gateway routing. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for data residency and cost predictability. Key asks: LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, proxy/gateway pattern, quota/rate-limit behavior, observability hooks and security (SOC2/KMS/SSO). Agreed next steps: share security pack, sample SDK snippets, estimate for 3-month pilot with reserved capacity and run a latency/cost micro-benchmark.
topics: Integration architecture: gateway/proxy vs sidecar vs direct SDK
Rate limits, tenant quotas and burst behavior
Observability hooks: traces, token-level cost, sampling
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (data residency, SLAs, cost)
Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack + SOC2 report link (Maya) - by 2027-08-12
Provide short SDK examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex (Carlos) - by 2027-08-13
Estimate pilot cost for 3 months reserved capacity + burst policy (Maya) - by 2027-08-15
Customer to share representative prompt set and traffic shape for pilot (Priya) - by 2027-08-14
Schedule 60m technical deep dive focused on observability and rate shaping (Carlos + Samir) - tentatively 2027-08-18
action_items: Maya Patel: Send security deck and link to SOC2 report (due 2027-08-12)
Carlos Ruiz: Create LangChain and LlamaIndex quickstart snippets and sample gateway config (due 2027-08-13)
Priya Menon: Share sample prompts, seq lengths, and 7-day traffic histogram (due 2027-08-14)
Maya Patel: Draft pilot pricing estimate with Dedicated reserved capacity and burst cap options (due 2027-08-15)
Samir Khatri: Compile security baseline questions re: KMS and on-prem HSM (due 2027-08-16)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Maya, Carlos (Redwood); Priya, Ethan, Samir, Lena (ClarityAI)
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for making time, quick intro — i'm maya redwood ae, carlos is our se. can you introduce yourselves?
[00:07] Priya (ClarityAI): yeah hi i'm priya head of ml at clarity ai, ethan platform, samir security, lena product. eager to understand integration story esp around langchain and proxy patterns.
[00:16] Maya: awesome, objective today is to map out how you'd wire Redwood in — hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs, sdk adapters, and observability. we'll also capture blockers.
[00:25] Ethan: high level, we run most workloads in us-east but we have eu data residency reqs for certain clients. for PII flows we need KMS control and audit logs. considering either hosted with VPC peering or private deployment.
[00:39] Samir: also SOC2, SSO via SAML, and we want RBAC integration with our idp. what's your bridge for that?
[00:47] Maya: Redwood supports SSO/SAML + SCIM and role mappings, audit logs stream to S3 or to your SIEM; for KMS we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM in Private. hosted can use Customer Key via cloud KMS in Dedicated plans. i'll send the security pack after this call.
[01:05] Lena: when you say private vs dedicated what's the real difference operationally?
[01:10] Carlos: good q — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in our infra with SLA for latency/uptime and data isolation; Private gives you a private control plane and can be VPC or on-prem where you manage KMS and network. Hosted is quickest but less isolated. dedicated is our middle ground for predictability.
[01:28] Priya: latency vs cost: for chat apps we need <200ms p50 ideally, but for batch embedding jobs we can tolerate seconds. how do you tune that?
[01:38] Carlos: we have batching, prefix/KV cache, and quantization profiles. for latency sensitive routes we disable batching or set tight batch windows; for embeddings we use bigger batch sizes to lower unit cost. you can pin routes to models/variants.
[01:52] Ethan: do you provide SDKs? we use LangChain in a few microservices and LlamaIndex for retrieval.
[01:58] Maya: yes — official SDKs in python/node with first-class LangChain connectors and LlamaIndex adapter examples. carlos will drop snippet. our gateway supports adapter configs so you can route requests from LangChain to hosted/dedicated/private without code changes.
[02:15] Samir: can you elaborate on gateway vs proxy vs sidecar? we have infra constraints and prefer not to change the runtime on all workers.
[02:23] Carlos: explained: proxy/gateway sits at the edge and routes traffic — good when you want centralized rate-limits and observability. sidecar is per-service and gives lower network hops and local caching. we also support SDK direct calls. common pattern: gateway for multi-tenant routing + sidecar for very high QPS internal services.
[02:42] Maya: important for you is quota enforcement — we do tenant quotas (tokens/min) and route-level caps, plus burst allowance that drains over time.
[02:50] Priya: how deterministic is the burst behavior? we can't have noisy neighbors causing >X throughput for a tenant.
[02:55] Carlos: we expose predictable throttles and leaky-bucket controls; with Dedicated you can have isolated pools eliminating noisy neighbor risk. for hosted we offer fair-share and can pin to dedicated variant on overflow.
[03:08] Ethan: tracing/observability — we need token-level cost, latencies per model, and sample of generation outputs for quality monitoring. how's that surfaced?
[03:16] Carlos: Console shows token-level cost, per-route latency histograms; we support OpenTelemetry traces and logs forwarded. sampling hook lets you capture 1% of generations to your storage. Also webhook hooks for completions.
[03:30] Priya: is there any PII redaction tooling on your side?
[03:33] Maya: we have content filters and can integrate pre/post-processing hooks in the gateway; but PII redaction is usually handled client-side or via a middleware we can help template.
[03:44] Lena: walk us through a simple LangChain flow — retrieval augmented generation: doc store -> llamaindex -> calls to model. where does Redwood sit?
[03:51] Carlos: you point the LangChain/LLamaIndex connector to Redwood SDK endpoint or gateway URL. request can include metadata headers for tenant id, route, and model preference. gateway can add KV-cache lookups to avoid repeated token costs for prefixes.
[04:07] Priya: the name is LlamaIndex or llama index in the SDK examples? we've seen casing differences in docs and it caused confusion earlier.
[04:12] Carlos: laughed, yes sometimes transcribed differently, we'll make sure examples match exact package names; snippet will reference "llama_index" and LangChain v0.2+ example.
[04:22] Ethan: about streaming — we need to stream partial tokens to clients; is that supported in private deploys?
[04:27] Maya: streaming is supported across deployments; for Private there is a streaming API that works over websockets or chunked-HTTP. latency depends on your network egress.
[04:36] Samir: security nit — for private deployments how do you handle signing and key rotation?
[04:40] Carlos: tokens are short-lived and signed; for Private we can integrate with your KMS for signing and automated rotation; we support HSM-backed keys via API.
[04:49] Priya: curious about model variants and fallbacks — if the requested model is out of capacity what happens?
[04:54] Maya: smart routing — policy-based fallback to smaller/quantized variants. we can route by latency or cost preference. dedicated pools have reserved capacity so less chance of fallbacks.
[05:06] Lena: any plugins for internal feature flags or rollout?
[05:09] Carlos: we have rollout policies and can do canary A/B at route level, traffic split for model versions, and automatic fallback if errors or latency cross threshold.
[05:20] Priya: can we bring our own fine-tuned model binary to private?
[05:24] Maya: yes for Private, you can bring model artifacts; we help with onboarding and advise quantization to balance latency.
[05:31] Ethan: instrumentation — do you emit spans with model name and token counts?
[05:35] Carlos: yes OpenTelemetry spans contain model, token usage, route id, and request/response timings. we also export metrics to Prometheus; console surfaces per-route cost.
[05:46] Samir: audit logs — retention and immutability?
[05:49] Maya: logs can be forwarded to customer S3 with lifecycle rules; for Private you can configure retention and immutability via your storage policies.
[05:58] Priya: any known limitations with LlamaIndex connectors on large retrievals? we've hit KV cache misses and memory blowups before.
[06:06] Carlos: LlamaIndex connector uses streaming chunking; we recommend chunk-size <= 1k tokens and using prefix/KV cache to avoid re-embedding identical contexts. We'll share tuning guide.
[06:17] Lena: okay what's the onboarding timeline if we want a pilot next month?
[06:21] Maya: for a hosted pilot you can be up in days. Dedicated pilot commonly takes 2-3 weeks for reserved pools and billing. Private (VPC) is 3-6 weeks depending on networking and KMS.
[06:33] Ethan: costs — we need a back-of-envelope to compare hosted vs dedicated for our peak 600 rps embedding traffic and 50 qps chat traffic.
[06:42] Maya: we asked for traffic shape in next steps — we'll produce a pilot estimate and a sampling benchmark to show p50/p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[06:53] Samir: legal/proc — do you have standard data processing agreement and addendums for EU data residency?
[06:58] Maya: yes DPA + EU addendum; i'll include links with the security pack.
[07:05] Priya: anything on rate limits with SDK — if a client hits rate limit what's the error pattern? 429 with retry-after?
[07:11] Carlos: 429 with Retry-After header, plus structured error body showing consumed tokens and remaining quota. we also support webhook alerts for quota nearing.
[07:21] Priya: what about client-side backoff recommendations?
[07:24] Carlos: exponential backoff suggested, we provide token bucket headers so clients can make smarter choices.
[07:31] Lena: observability hooks again — can we add custom tags per request for product-level dashboards?
[07:36] Carlos: yes pass X-Route-Tag or similar, those show up in console filters and traces.
[07:42] Samir: do you retain response bodies for debugging?
[07:45] Maya: by default we retain minimal telemetry; response captures are opt-in and can be sampled or forwarded to your storage. retention policy in the security pack.
[07:56] Priya: ok let's surface a simple integration flow: LangChain app calls Redwood gateway -> gateway applies KV cache and quota -> routes to dedicated pool -> returns streaming tokens. who owns the cache?
[08:06] Carlos: gateway-managed prefix and KV cache. for sidecar pattern cache is local to service. we also support external redis for shared caches.
[08:16] Ethan: do you have a proxy image we can spin in our k8s cluster?
[08:19] Carlos: yes lightweight proxy image in GitHub — we'll share helm chart and example values for rate limits and envoy integration.
[08:27] Priya: will that be compatible with our service mesh? we use istio.
[08:31] Carlos: we have istio examples — sidecar compatibility tested. proxy sits as a gateway service behind ingress.
[08:39] Lena: demo request — can we get a short demo of SDK + gateway config for a simple RAG flow?
[08:44] Maya: sure — we'll do a demo during the technical deep dive.
[08:48] Samir: we need to vet telemetry: are traces PII safe?
[08:52] Carlos: traces can be redacted; we recommend hashing or removing PII before sending. we can work with you to define redaction rules.
[08:59] Priya: what's the strategy for handling model drift and quality regressions?
[09:03] Maya: Redwood Optimize ties evals to deployments — you can run golden prompt sets and get regression alerts if metrics drop; automatic rollback is available for routes.
[09:14] Ethan: how do we measure token-level cost per feature?
[09:18] Carlos: console gives token breakdown per route and per-token pricing; you can tag requests with feature id to attribute costs.
[09:25] Lena: ok wrapping — recapped asks?
[09:28] Maya: recap: we'll send security pack, SDK snippets, pilot estimate; customer to share prompts & traffic. plan technical deep dive for observability and quotas.
[09:40] Priya: agreed. thanks everyone.
[09:43] Maya: i'll follow up with calendar invite and links.
[09:46] End of recording.
